input_text: Joe is being prosecuted for illegally transporting turtle eggs under an animal trafficking statute. To prove that Joe owned the duffel bag in which contained the turtle eggs, the prosecution introduces evidence of Joe asking a store-owner if they carried any duffel bags.

extraction.input_text: Joe is being prosecuted for illegally transporting turtle eggs under an animal trafficking statute. To prove that Joe owned the duffel bag in which contained the turtle eggs, the prosecution introduces evidence of Joe asking a store-owner if they carried any duffel bags.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: Joe's inquiry to the store-owner about duffel bags was made outside of the courtroom proceedings.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(1) - Hearsay requires an out-of-court statement.
arguments.evidence_span: Joe asking a store-owner if they carried any duffel bags.

arguments.text: The statement is a question, which is generally considered non-assertive under FRE 801(a)(3) and thus falls outside the definition of hearsay.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a)(3) - A statement must be an 'assertion' to be hearsay; questions are typically non-assertive.
arguments.evidence_span: Joe asking a store-owner if they carried any duffel bags.

arguments.text: The prosecution introduces the statement to prove that Joe owned the duffel bag containing the turtle eggs, which constitutes offering it for the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c)(2) - Hearsay requires the statement be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted.
arguments.evidence_span: To prove that Joe owned the duffel bag in which contained the turtle eggs, the prosecution introduces evidence of Joe asking a store-owner if they carried any duffel bags.

arguments.text: The evidence is circumstantial and relies on Joe's conduct rather than an out-of-court assertion, meaning it does not depend on the declarant's sincerity or accuracy.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a)(3) & Evidence Principles - Non-assertive conduct or circumstantial evidence is not hearsay because it does not rely on the declarant's sincerity.
arguments.evidence_span: Joe asking a store-owner if they carried any duffel bags.

arguments.text: The statement is Joe's own statement offered against him in a criminal case, which is excluded from the hearsay definition under FRE 801(d)(2)(A).
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(d)(2)(A) - A statement offered against an opposing party and made by the party is not hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: Joe is being prosecuted... the prosecution introduces evidence of Joe asking a store-owner...
